note: Season-end tryouts and the first transfer opportunity (spec §18, §20). These scenes read tryout state — invitations, sessions played, offers, kept and broken promises, the accepted club, where the friend lands — and never create it: src/campaign/tryouts.ts issues invitations and offers from verified evidence and roster capacity, and the transfer happens only when the user accepts an offer in the hub. Boys'/girls' entries override same-id shared scenes. Every line is a proposal for the owner's review.

lines.text: Monday. The season is over and the fridge calendar has exactly one thing on it, circled twice: Saturday {tryout_day}. Tryouts.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Two sessions on the day — morning and afternoon. You can go to two clubs, or one, or none. Every club in the valley is holding one.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: {invited_clubs} asked for you by name. That's nice. It's still an invitation, not a place.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Nobody asked for you by name. That's fine. Open sessions are open. You turn up and play.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: And {club} doesn't need you to try out. {coach} already said what {coach} thinks, to your face. Hold on to that.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Whatever you pick, I pick. I said that already. I'm not un-saying it.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: You're going to look. Fine. I'm coming to watch. Somebody has to heckle the goalkeeper.

choices.label: "I want to play. Every minute I can."

response.speaker: parent
response.text: Then look at their benches on Saturday, not their kits.

choices.label: "I want to get better. Whoever coaches best."

response.speaker: parent
response.text: Then listen to how they talk to the kid who gets it wrong. That's the coaching.

choices.label: "I want to be where my people are."

response.speaker: parent
response.text: That's allowed. Just make sure it's your reason and not somebody else's.

lines.text: Saturday. Five clubs, one complex, a hundred kids in five colours of bib, and somebody's dad with a clipboard nobody gave him.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Pick your sessions from the board. Watch how they coach, not just how they look. I'll be by the fence with the bad coffee.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Okay. Same sessions or split up and compare notes?

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: I'm on the fence with {parent}. Literally. Go show them the thing you do.
The thing about a tryout is that nobody has seen your season. They see today. Play it.
Sunday evening. The phone has been face down on the table since dinner and everyone has been pretending not to look at it.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: One offer. {offers}. A real one — a place on a roster, in writing, with a date to answer by.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: {offer_count} offers. {offers}. Real ones — a place on a roster, in writing, with a date to answer by.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: {coach} rang as well. {club} wants you back. That's an offer too, not a hint.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: {coach} didn't ring. I'd rather that than a promise nobody meant.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: {broken_club} promised and then didn't. Keep that in a drawer somewhere. It's useful.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Nothing decides itself. You've got a week, and the offers will be there in the morning.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: So? SO?

choices.label: Talk it through with {friend} before deciding anything

response.speaker: friend
response.text: Good. Because I've got a list. It's colour-coded. Don't laugh.

response.speaker: parent
response.text: I'd pick the place that keeps its small promises. The big ones are easy to say.
The offers are on the fridge under a magnet, next to the calendar. Circled once this time.

lines.text: Sunday evening. The phone stays face down and stays quiet.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: No offers. Not from Saturday — and not from {club} either.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: {broken_club} promised you a place. I heard it. So did you. That wasn't an offer, and now we both know the difference.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: I'm not going to pretend that doesn't sting. It does. It's also May, and nothing about you has stopped.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Rec league has a team. I checked. I'm on it if you are.

choices.label: "The sessions were fair. I wasn't there yet."

response.speaker: parent
response.text: That's the hardest sentence there is, and you just said it at eleven.

response.speaker: parent
response.text: Maybe. Sleep, and tell me again in the morning if you still believe it.

lines.text: The drive home from the complex. The radio is off; nobody turned it off, it's just off.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: {broken_club}'s coach told you there was a place for you. Told me too, by the fence. Then the sheet went up and your name wasn't on it.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: I'm not saying they lied. Squads fill. I'm saying a promise is a sentence and an offer is a piece of paper, and you only ever count the paper.

response.speaker: parent
response.text: Write that on something. You'll need it at fourteen, and again at eighteen.

response.speaker: parent
response.text: Maybe they did. Be angry tonight. Tomorrow, look at what's actually on the fridge.

lines.text: The training field with no training on it. {coach} is collecting cones that were already collected.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good. I meant what I said in April and I mean it now. August. Come back a year better and we'll see what this team is.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You had a real offer and you turned it down for us. I won't waste that.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Same team. SAME TEAM. I'm not crying, the sprinklers are on.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: You stayed and I'm going. That's — yeah. That's a weird one. Park's still the park though.
The car, after. The form is signed and in the glovebox because nobody trusts a bag.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: {next_club}. Say it out loud so it's real.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: {coach} shook your hand and meant it. No grudges from that one, ever. That's rarer than you think.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: You're going. Okay. Okay. Sundays at the park still stand — that was never a club thing.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Same club, new badge. I've already worked out the car-share. You're welcome.

choices.label: Text {coach} a proper thank-you, not a short one

response.speaker: parent
response.text: That's how you leave a place. Well done.

response.speaker: parent
response.text: Fair. Just send the text sometime this week. Forward doesn't mean rude.

lines.text: The park. The goal with the bent post. Neither of you has said the thing yet.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: So. {friend_club} for me, {next_club} for you.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: We'll play each other. You know that, right? Like, actually against. I'm going to be so annoying.
The ball comes back off the bent post the way it always has. Some things don't check which club you're at.

immediate.text: Sundays at the park with {friend}, whatever club either of you plays for.

response.speaker: friend
response.text: Deal. And if you miss one I'm telling {parent}.

response.speaker: friend
response.text: Yeah. Different isn't worse. Probably. Kick it, I'm cold.

lines.text: The park. The goal with the bent post. Somebody is doing a victory lap of it for no reason.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: {friend_club}. Both of us. I said whatever you pick, I pick, and then I had to actually go and earn it, which, rude.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: New kit, same bent post. Kick it.
The offers on the fridge have a date on them. It was yesterday.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: They lapsed. Nobody's roster has your name on it for August — not because you weren't wanted. Because you didn't answer.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: That's a lesson too. It's just a more expensive one than I'd have picked.

response.speaker: parent
response.text: It is. Summer's long. We'll find you somewhere to play.

lines.text: The last offer is turned down. The car is quiet for three streets.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: So that's every club told no — including ours. You know that means no roster for August.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: I'm not angry. I just want to hear the reason from you, not guess at it.

choices.label: "None of them felt right. I'd rather wait than pick wrong."

response.speaker: parent
response.text: Then we wait together. Summer sessions still happen; I'll drive.

response.speaker: parent
response.text: That's honest. Honest we can work with. Nobody's closing a door on a ten-year-old for good.

lines.text: The park. The goal with the bent post. {friend} is doing a victory lap of it for no reason.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: {friend_club}. Both of us. I said whatever you pick, I pick, and then I had to actually go and earn it, which, rude.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: First training I'm nutmegging you in front of the new lot. Just so you know it's coming.
The park. The goal with the bent post. {friend} has drawn the new badge on the back of her hand in biro.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: {friend_club}. Both of us. I said whatever you pick, I pick, and then I had to actually go and earn it, which, rude.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: I've already made a playlist for the drive. It's mostly one song. You'll like it eventually.
